chapter: New Orleans arrival, jazz and Fazola
title: Friendship with Fazola, his popularity and funeral
summary: Mazzari knew Fazola only about a year, played jobs and visited clubs with him, saw how musicians lit up when he arrived, and was struck by the flowers from big-name bands at his funeral.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: How long did you know Fazz before he died?
Oh, let's see. I think I only know him about a year. I had just met him and just began a good friendship with him, you know.
Were you with him pretty steady?

Well, I always wound up playing jobs, you know, in the same band and several times, well, you know, Fazz, he was, he was so popular that people would just beg him, I said, please come down to my joint and play even if it's only, all right.

a couple of tunes or something, you know. And he would. I mean, he'd try to go to all these places, but if he tried to go to all of them, there wouldn't be enough time in the day. So he tried to make the few ones that he could, and he asked me if I would care to go along with him, you know. And I said, sure. So I learned a lot by going after him, and I learned how popular he was and how well he played, and I got to know a lot of things about him that I didn't know. And he really was. I mean, you could tell when he walked into a place, even if it was to play a set, maybe, you know. Boy, the joint would really start getting a feel, you know. He was a very remarkable guy.
How did the other musicians react when he came here?

Oh, they'd just break out in a big smile, you know. If they had been bored, well, they weren't bored anymore when he walked in, I'll tell you that. The guy actually would throw sunshine. That's how good he was. Not only his plane, but his personality. He was a nice guy. He really was. He was a good Joe. Just ate too much, huh? Yeah, too many oysters. I guess.
I think that's what killed him. I'm not sure. All that easy.

Well, I suppose, ooh, too much beer, too. I suppose. I don't know. But I was surprised when I went to the funeral. He had got flowers from famous bandsmen, you know, throughout the country. And, I mean, the big-name bands all sent flowers. And he had people at his funeral. It was fantastic. Well, anyway, that's how I got to meet people from New Orleans, you know. And I really enjoyed it. I really got the feel of what New Orleans is, you know. What New Orleans jazz is.
